title: Pixtral Large 2502 API Pricing: Cost per 1M Tokens
summary: Pixtral Large 2502 api pricing details allow developers to forecast monthly operational expenses for multimodal workflows.
body_markdown:
## Comparing pixtral large 2502 vision costs


Pixtral Large 2502 has a better performance-to-price ratio for high-resolution image reasoning. It outperforms GPT-6.2 Astra or Claude Sonnet 5.5 in this specific metric.


The efficiency with which the model processes visual data means you pay for fewer total tokens to achieve the same level of analytical accuracy.


This remains true even if the $2 per million token rate for input appears high on a standard text-based spreadsheet, suggesting that the long-term value of the model may be obscured by simple unit-cost comparisons.


### How image tokenization affects Pixtral billing


It tokenizes images based on their actual information density rather than a fixed grid.


"Token bloat" common in models like GPT-6.2 Sol is prevented by this approach. In those models, high-resolution files are subdivided into numerous 512-pixel tiles that each incur a flat fee regardless of the visual complexity.


By mapping visual features directly to a latent space, Pixtral ensures a high-contrast architectural diagram costs less to process than a dense, multi-page spreadsheet. You can then predict costs based on data complexity rather than just file size.


### Pixtral Large 2502 cost per document extraction


When you're processing large batches of technical documents, the cost efficiency of Pixtral Large 2502 becomes evident through its reduced need for multi-shot prompting.


Competitive models like Gemini 4 Argon often require three or four example images in the prompt to maintain structural integrity in the output, which triples the per-request cost for every extraction.


Fields in a complex invoice or blueprint are identified in a single pass thanks to Pixtral’s zero-shot capabilities. The effective price per successful extraction remains lower than competitors that charge less per token but require more tokens to reach a usable result.


### Pixtral Large 2502 vs Gemini 3.1 Pro benchmarks


Pixtral Large 2502 outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on specialized visual reasoning tasks, proving that higher intelligence at the edge of the frontier reduces the long-term cost of error correction.


> The effective price per successful extraction remains lower than competitors that charge less per token but require more tokens to reach a usable result.


The MathVista benchmark, which tests the ability to interpret charts and mathematical diagrams, shows Pixtral reaching **69.4% accuracy** , surpassing the 68.1% mark set by Gemini 1.5 Pro, establishing a new performance baseline for multimodal reasoning, which means the model is now the state-of-the-art leader for complex visual tasks.


MathVista benchmark scores: 69.4% for Pixtral vs 68.1% for Gemini 1.5 Pro.


For every thousand documents processed, Pixtral identifies thirteen more correct data points than its closest rival. This margin of accuracy reduces the manual labor costs associated with human-in-the-loop verification.


Consequently, the premium you pay for the initial inference is recovered by the reduction in secondary auditing requirements.
